$100,000 in 1986 to create NeXT’s identity, but the fee came with an unusual stipulation that Jobs would get one solution and not a selection of alternatives.
Rand Refused To Offer Jobs Options

In a 1993 interview, Jobs recalled asking for several options. Rand refused. "No, I will solve your problem for you and you will pay me," Jobs quoted him as saying. "You don’t have to use the solution. If you want options go talk to other people."

. Rand initially hesitated because
IBM
was a client. "Initially I told Jobs I couldn’t do it because he was competing with one of my accounts," Rand recalled in a 1989 profile. Jobs secured IBM’s blessing and the assignment proceeded.
IBM says Rand redesigned its logo in 1956 and produced the eight-bar identity in 1972. He also created identities for
UPS
and
ABC
. Jobs later called him "the greatest living graphic designer."

children: NeXT Logo Becomes Jobs’ ‘Little Jewel’
Rand turned NeXT into a tilted black cube carrying the company name and explained his reasoning in a presentation booklet.

"He solved a very difficult problem for us," Jobs said in the 1993 interview. Most companies, he argued, had only a logotype, while a rare few possessed a symbol recognizable on its own. Apple already had that advantage because its symbol and name were the same thing.
Jobs said building that association normally took "10 years and $100 million."

"Our challenge was, How could we have a little jewel that we could use without the name to put on the product?" Jobs said. Rand’s answer was "a little jewel that had contained in it the name of the company."
